title: Sharing into whole groups with //
idea: // divides and keeps only the whole part — how many full groups you can make.

exercises.prompt: You have 7 cookies to share into groups of 3. How many FULL groups of 3 can you make?
exercises.explanation: 3 + 3 = 6 cookies make 2 full groups. The 7th cookie can't make another group of 3. So 2 full groups.

exercises.prompt:
The // sign means 'divide and keep only the whole part'. What will this show?

print(7 // 3)
exercises.explanation: 7 // 3 asks how many whole 3s fit in 7. Two 3s fit (that's 6). So it shows 2. The leftover is ignored by //.

exercises.prompt: // always gives a whole number, never something like 2.5
exercises.explanation: That's the whole point of //. It keeps only the whole part of the division, so the result is always a whole number.
Two fits into 10 exactly five times. 10 // 2 is 5. When it divides evenly, // gives the same answer as regular division.
How many whole 4s fit in 9? Two (that's 8), and 1 is left over. // keeps only the whole part: 2.
// keeps only the whole part — the number of full groups. A single / keeps the fraction too.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the blank so this shows how many whole 5s fit in 17.

print(17 __ 5)
exercises.explanation: 17 // 5 is 3, because three 5s make 15 and fit inside 17. // gives the whole count.

exercises.prompt: 8 // 2 and 8 / 2 both give 4 here, because 8 shares evenly into 2s.
exercises.explanation: When the division is exact, // and / land on the same number. The difference shows up only when there's a leftover.

exercises.prompt: Match each // expression to what it shows.
exercises.explanation: Each asks 'how many whole copies fit?' Two fits 3 times in 6; four, five, and six each fit just once.

exercises.prompt: A pizza has 12 slices. Four friends share it into equal whole slices each. Which line finds slices per friend?
exercises.explanation: 12 // 4 is 3 — each friend gets 3 whole slices. You just used // to share into whole groups!
